## Summary

Jonas, Kęstutis's armour-bearer and pack-elder (*vilkų vyresnysis*) of the hidden nine, is the Loyal Hound of Book I, the oldest surviving [Iron Wolf](../factions/iron_wolves.qmd) of Kęstutis's guard. "Jonas" is a skin-name (*kailio vardas*): the baptismal name of an Order sergeant he killed at the gate in 1361 during Kęstutis's escape from Marienburg, worn as a trophy, which is why a pagan wolf has a saint's name. He serves the son because he swore to the father, leaves a horse at an oak for the fleeing Vytautas, leads the remnant band in 1384 and dies under the oak.

## Appearance & tells

Grey-bearded, broad and quiet, in wolf-hide over quilted wool, no plate. His mark is the burned palm, the pack-elder's brand, from carrying the pack's single feast-day iron blade wrapped in linen. He does not drink Jogaila's mead and will not drink from a hand that has not given bread (Book I ch. 2). Part of his soul stays wolf.

## Want · Need · Lie · Truth

| | |
|---|---|
| **Want** (external) | To keep the oath he swore to Kęstutis by serving the son. |
| **Need** (internal) | To be told that the old law has an end, and that it may be broken without dying. |
| **Lie** they believe | That the Pack's Word is the whole of the law. |
| **Truth** they learn (or refuse) | That a wolf's law can be kept by the prince: Vytautas does not burn him but carries him to a bog (Book I ch. 25). |

## Arc by book

- **Book VI (1361):** the young wolf who kills an Order sergeant at Marienburg's last gate and takes his Christian name (ch. 18, POV); at Rudau (ch. 24); in the epilogue (ch. 30).
- **Book I (1382-84):** among the hidden nine at Kęstutis's side (ch. 2); the silver wolf goes to Vytautas; is not in the tents when the guard is slaughtered at Jogaila's camp (ch. 7; seven of the nine die there, Jonas's men stayed in Kęstutis's own camp, canon D10); leaves a horse for the fleeing Vytautas at a named oak (ch. 15); leads the band at the burning of the Order's castles in July 1384 and dies under the oak (ch. 25).

## Power & magic

Granted, the **Wolf-Change** ([Vilkų krikštas](../magic/wolf_change.qmd)) from the Root-Mother via the Dykra: night-sight, scent, fast healing, the berserk "iron hour". Vilkatai are not casters and sit outside the tier ladder; the graph gives tier 3 to the wolf-change. He lives by the Pack's Word and by its nine laws, one of which, no Gediminid blood, is the Pact's. Part of his soul stays wolf.

## Record vs saga

- **[Record]:** No such person in the record. The 1361 escape is real (Kęstutis fled Marienburg on 11 Nov 1361 with a servant, Alf, who removed bricks from the cell wall; veidas.lt, VLE); the Order sergeant at the gate, and Jonas, are the saga's.
- **[Saga invention]:** All of him: the skin-name, the burned palm, the hidden nine, the horse at the oak, the band of 1384. Book VI ch. 18 (his POV) shows how he took the name.

## Pronunciation

**JO-nas** (/ˈjoːnɐs/), English respelling *YOH-nahs*. Paradigm 2: instrumental *Jonù* and locative *Jonè* are end-stressed; elsewhere the stress is on *JO-*. [world_rules/pronunciation_lexicon.json]

## Appearances

**Book I:** ch. 2, 4, 7, 8, 12, 13, 15, 25. **Book VI:** ch. 18 (POV), 24, 30 and the afterword. Not to be confused with Jonas Alšėniškis (Book II) or [Jonas Goštautas](gostautas.qmd).
